_comment: Category rules, applied by scripts/harvest.py in the order given. A host is matched whole and its subdomains come with it, so a rule on `plex.tv` already covers `proxy.plex.tv`. The first matching rule wins, so put specific rules above general ones. `category` must be a name from the vocabulary in scripts/catalog-core.py; `service` is optional and names an entry in seeds/services.json.

rules.note: Media servers and the *arr family: one product each, not one company.
Developer package registries and tool vendors from proxy exception lists.
Microsoft application platform and developer infrastructure.
Linear TV platforms.
Video player vendors. Brightcove and Conviva are sold to broadcasters, but what a person sees is a video stream.
Turner Broadcasting / CBS.
Directv.
Affiliate networks and ad servers. These are what an allowlist is mostly made of.
Ad servers a person never meets by name. Deliberately ads, not analytics: a retargeting host is still an ad host.
Measurement and product analytics endpoints.
Microsoft identity, connectivity check and update hosts. The NCSI names answer 'is there internet' and belong to no product a person recognises.
Bing Maps tiles and the VirtualEarth endpoints behind them.
Amazon's own short domain and its OCSP responder.
Third-party CDN vendors whose names a person has never heard of.
Media metadata and audience measurement: the databases and analytics a streaming app reads.
OneDrive, the product behind 1drv.com.
Developer and utility hosts that appear in real traffic and mean nothing to a user.
Marketing chat and support widgets.
Broadcasters that are not one of the big five: SBS is an Australian public broadcaster, so its streams are video.
ThePlatform and DigitalSmiths are video delivery vendors, sold to broadcasters.
TED, including its own CDN.
Spotify's own CDN, under both the .co and .com names.
Microsoft-owned games and game networks.
Microsoft-owned communication and mailbox products.
Bing search and Microsoft Start/news surfaces.
LinkedIn social graph and media hosts.
Microsoft AI services and products.
Electric JCDecaux: transit advertising and real-time departure boards.
WordPress.
abuse.ch malware trackers.
NVIDIA GeForce.
The Android connectivity check answers 'is there internet' and belongs to no product.
Amazon's link shortener; the destination is Amazon, so it files as shopping.
Driftt is a travel operator, which is a different company from Drift, the chat widget.
URL shorteners. `other` is the honest answer: a shortener is not a thing a person uses on purpose.

drop._comment: Hosts deliberately not added. A wrong label is worse than no label, because it looks authoritative; these are parked, thrown away, or are lists rather than services. Keep the reason — an unexplained drop is indistinguishable from an oversight.
